title: Exposure of account registration identifiers during onboarding
description: During account registration, the Home Hub may collect and receive directly identifying information such as name, email address, phone number, home address, account username, or household identifiers. If this data flow is intercepted, over-collected, or stored without minimization, the homeowner can be identified from the onboarding data.
assumptions: The registration flow includes personal account attributes, not just anonymous device pairing.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id only; exact LINDDUN Pro subtree for direct identifiability may vary by catalog version.

title: Linkability between homeowner identity and enrolled devices
description: The flow binds the homeowner account to specific cameras and sensors. Device serial numbers, MAC addresses, model identifiers, and installation metadata can be linked to the same person or household over time, enabling correlation of multiple devices and activities to a single homeowner.
assumptions: Enrollment transmits persistent device identifiers together with account or household identifiers.
uncertainty_note: Node id is a best-fit estimate for linkability via persistent identifiers.

title: Detection of smart-home ownership and occupancy patterns from enrollment traffic
description: Observing this onboarding flow may reveal that the household owns a home-security system, cameras, or sensors, and may disclose when setup occurs. Even without reading full contents, metadata such as timing, frequency, or device type indicators can let an observer detect the existence of the system and infer household characteristics.
assumptions: An attacker or third party can observe network metadata or partially inspect traffic.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id only; exact detectability subtree may differ.

title: Disclosure of sensitive household and device configuration data
description: Enrollment may disclose sensitive data such as device inventory, device locations, camera names, room labels, network credentials, home topology, and security preferences. Unauthorized disclosure of this setup information can reveal intimate details about the home and facilitate further surveillance or attack.
assumptions: The setup flow includes configuration details beyond minimal pairing metadata.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id; specific disclosure subtype may vary by LINDDUN Pro version.

title: Insufficient transparency about onboarding data use
description: The homeowner may not understand what personal data and device metadata are collected during registration and enrollment, how long they are retained, whether they are shared with cloud services or third parties, or which data are optional versus mandatory. This undermines user awareness and informed privacy decisions.
assumptions: The flow or interface lacks clear privacy notice and granular explanations during setup.
uncertainty_note: Node id is a best-fit estimate for lack of user awareness/transparency.

title: Invalid or non-granular consent for device enrollment data processing
description: If the Home Hub requires blanket acceptance to register an account and enroll devices, the homeowner may be unable to selectively consent to collection of device metadata, analytics, cloud synchronization, or sharing with service partners. Processing may therefore occur without freely given, specific, informed, and unambiguous consent.
assumptions: Consent is used as a legal basis and setup does not provide granular, optional choices.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id only; exact non-compliance/consent subtree may differ.

title: Lack of provable homeowner consent or action records for registration and enrollment
description: If the system does not securely log that the homeowner registered the account, accepted privacy choices, and initiated enrollment of each camera or sensor, either party may later be unable to prove what was agreed or performed. This can create disputes about whether a device was intentionally enrolled or whether privacy notices and choices were presented.
assumptions: Audit trails for consent and enrollment events are weak, mutable, or absent.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id; repudiation-related subtree naming may vary.

title: Guest access-code submissions can be linked to a specific guest over time
description: If the Home Hub stores or transmits the temporary access code together with timestamps, device identifiers, door-unlock outcomes, or network metadata, repeated uses of the code may be linked to the same guest or visit pattern. This can allow reconstruction of when a guest arrived, how often they visited, and correlation with other household events.
assumptions: Assumes the Home Hub logs code-entry events or associated metadata beyond what is strictly needed for immediate verification.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id; exact LINDDUN Pro linkage subtree labeling may vary.

title: Temporary access code can disclose guest association or presence
description: The temporary code and its use may reveal that a particular guest has been invited, is currently present, or was present at a given time. If exposed through logs, notifications, backups, or insecure transmission inside the hub ecosystem, this information can disclose social relationships and occupancy patterns.
assumptions: Assumes the code or event data is observable to parties beyond the guest and the minimal verification component.
uncertainty_note: Node id is a best-effort estimate for information disclosure of provided credentials and associated event data.

title: Code-entry events may enable detection of guest presence
description: Observing the flow of a guest entering a temporary code at the Home Hub can let an attacker detect that someone is at the door or that a guest visit is occurring, even without knowing the guest's identity. Traffic patterns, interface activation, unlock attempts, or notifications may expose this event.
assumptions: Assumes side-channel observation is possible through network traffic, local observation, telemetry, or notifications.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit detectability node id; exact subtree may differ depending on whether observation is local or network-based.

title: Guest may be unable to plausibly deny entering the code
description: If the Home Hub records precise code-entry attempts, timestamps, success/failure status, or binds temporary codes to named guests, the resulting evidence may prevent the guest from denying that they attempted entry or entered at a particular time. This can create privacy risk where visit confidentiality is expected.
assumptions: Assumes logs are retained and attributable to a specific guest or temporary code assignment.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for non-repudiation caused by attributable event logging.

title: Guest may be unaware of logging and secondary use of access-code data
description: The guest may not be informed that the Home Hub logs temporary code entry, associates it with identity or visit metadata, retains failed attempts, or shares events with cloud services, app users, or third-party integrations. Lack of visibility undermines user awareness of how personal data from the interaction is processed.
assumptions: Assumes the system does not provide clear notice at the point of code entry.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for insufficient user awareness/transparency.

title: Processing of temporary access-code data may exceed consent or reasonable expectation
description: The guest may provide the code solely to unlock the door, while the Home Hub or connected services also use the data for analytics, behavior profiling, long-term retention, security scoring, or sharing with other parties. Such secondary processing may occur without valid consent or another appropriate legal basis.
assumptions: Assumes code-entry data is reused beyond immediate access control or retained longer than necessary.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for non-compliance/consent-lawfulness issues; exact subtree may vary by jurisdiction and implementation.

title: Linkability of household activity patterns across logged sensor events
description: A local event log that stores motion, door, and other sensor events over time can allow events to be linked to the same household, device set, room, or occupant behavior pattern. Even if individual entries seem innocuous, the log can reveal recurring routines such as wake/sleep times, occupancy, and comings and goings.
assumptions: The log retains identifiers, timestamps, device names, room labels, or other stable attributes across entries.
uncertainty_note: Tree node id is a best-effort selection for generic linkability in a data store; exact LINDDUN Pro subnode may vary.

title: Identifiability of residents from detailed local event history
description: Fine-grained event records from doors, motion sensors, and similar devices may enable identification of specific residents or visitors by their movement patterns, schedules, or association with particular rooms/devices, especially when combined with household context.
assumptions: The log contains sufficiently detailed timestamps and sensor metadata to distinguish behavior patterns.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort node id for identifiability; exact subnode may differ depending on whether the focus is direct identifiers or quasi-identifying behavioral data.

title: Disclosure of private household behavior through local event log contents
description: The event log stores sensitive information about presence, absence, room usage, entry/exit events, and daily routines. Unauthorized access to the local log could disclose intimate details of household life, including when the home is empty or when particular areas are used.
assumptions: An attacker, insider, or other unauthorized party could access the local datastore or backups.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort node id for information disclosure from data at rest in a datastore.

title: Residents may be unable to repudiate inferred activities recorded by the hub
description: When the Home Hub writes sensor events into the local log, those records may later be treated as evidence that a resident opened a door, moved in a room, or was present at a certain time. Because sensor inferences can be imperfect and occupants may not control logging, individuals may be unable to deny actions or presence inferred from the recorded events.
assumptions: The log is used for audit, troubleshooting, automation review, or other later decision-making.
uncertainty_note: Repudiation is somewhat indirect here because the log captures sensor events rather than explicit user statements; node id is best-effort.

title: Unawareness of extent and sensitivity of event logging
description: Occupants may be unaware that the Home Hub persistently writes motion, door, and sensor events to a local datastore, how long they are kept, and what inferences can be drawn from them. This lack of awareness undermines informed privacy expectations.
assumptions: The system provides limited notice or unclear explanations about local logging, retention, and access.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort node id for unawareness relating to collection/storage transparency.

title: Non-compliance risk from excessive or unjustified retention of local sensor events
description: Persistently storing detailed household sensor events in the local log may violate privacy requirements or policies if retention exceeds necessity, purpose limitation is unclear, or adequate safeguards and user controls are missing.
assumptions: Applicable privacy requirements, internal policies, or user promises constrain retention, minimization, transparency, or access controls.
uncertainty_note: Exact compliance obligations depend on jurisdiction and product commitments; node id is best-effort for generic non-compliance.

title: Detectability of occupancy and routine from existence and timing of log entries
description: Even without reading full event contents, the mere presence, timing, frequency, or volume of writes to the local event log can reveal when sensors are active, when people are moving, or when doors are opened, allowing an observer to detect occupancy or notable household events.
assumptions: An observer can monitor the datastore, metadata, or write patterns without necessarily seeing all plaintext contents.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort node id for detectability based on metadata and event occurrence rather than full disclosure.

title: Upload metadata can reveal household routines
description: When the Home Hub uploads recorded camera clips, timestamps, clip frequency, camera identifiers, and event-trigger patterns can reveal when occupants are home, asleep, away, or moving through specific areas. Even if clip content is protected, the upload behavior itself can disclose sensitive personal information.
assumptions: The cloud service or intermediaries can observe upload timing, size, frequency, or associated metadata.
uncertainty_note: Node id is my best fit for disclosure of information via observable metadata; exact LINDDUN Pro subtree labeling may differ.

title: Stored video clips expose highly sensitive in-home activities
description: Cloud Video Storage contains recorded camera clips from inside or around a home. Unauthorized access, overly broad internal access, or weak isolation could disclose occupants' identities, behavior, visitors, possessions, and daily activities.
assumptions: Video clips may contain identifiable people and intimate household context.
uncertainty_note: Tree node is best-estimate for direct disclosure of stored content; exact node id may vary in LINDDUN Pro.

title: Video clips can be linked across time to build occupant profiles
description: A persistent cloud repository of clips enables linking multiple recordings from the same household, camera, account, and time periods. This can produce detailed longitudinal profiles of residents, routines, relationships, and behavior patterns.
assumptions: Clips are associated with stable account, device, or household identifiers in storage or indexing systems.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort node id for linkability through stable identifiers and accumulated records.

title: Cloud-stored clips enable identifying residents and visitors
description: Faces, voices, clothing, location context, and associated account metadata in uploaded clips can directly or indirectly identify household members, guests, neighbors, or passersby.
assumptions: Clip content or metadata is accessible to the cloud provider, authorized staff, attackers, or third parties under some conditions.
uncertainty_note: Node id is my best fit for identifiability from content and metadata.

title: Users may be unaware of the extent of cloud upload and retention
description: Occupants or visitors may not understand that recordings are uploaded off-device to cloud storage, how long they are retained, who can access them, or whether they are reused for analytics or service improvement. This undermines informed expectations and meaningful transparency.
assumptions: Not all affected individuals are clearly notified about cloud storage practices.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort node id for unawareness/transparency concerns; exact subtree may differ.

title: Cloud storage of home video may exceed consent or purpose expectations
description: Uploading and retaining home camera clips in cloud storage may go beyond what residents, visitors, or bystanders reasonably consented to, especially if the clips are later accessed for secondary purposes such as analytics, sharing, or law-enforcement response.
assumptions: Consent from all affected data subjects may be absent, ambiguous, or limited to narrower purposes than cloud retention.
uncertainty_note: Tree node is a best estimate for non-compliance/consent-purpose-limitation issues.

title: Lack of verifiable upload and access records can undermine accountability
description: If the cloud storage service does not maintain trustworthy logs of which clips were uploaded, when, by whom they were accessed, and whether they were altered or deleted, parties may later be unable to prove or dispute privacy-impacting actions. This weakens accountability around handling sensitive home video.
assumptions: Audit logging or integrity protection for logs may be insufficient.
uncertainty_note: Repudiation is less central than disclosure here; node id is a best-effort mapping to lack of accountability/non-repudiation.

title: Excessive retention of uploaded clips enables over-collection over time
description: Storing uploaded home video clips for long periods increases the volume and sensitivity of personal data held about the household. This creates a larger privacy impact than necessary for the immediate monitoring purpose and amplifies harm if the data is later disclosed or repurposed.
assumptions: Retention periods may be long or indefinite by default.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for data minimization/retention concerns; exact LINDDUN Pro numbering may differ.

title: Motion-alert messages may be linkable to the same household or device over time
description: Repeated real-time motion alerts sent from the Home Hub to the backend can contain stable identifiers, network metadata, routing tokens, or characteristic event patterns that allow the backend or anyone with access to logs to link multiple alerts to the same home, device, or occupants over time.
assumptions: The flow carries a persistent hub, account, household, or session identifier, or otherwise exposes stable metadata enabling correlation.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort node selection for linkability of messages/metadata; exact LINDDUN Pro subtree label may vary by catalog edition.

title: Motion alerts may identify a specific household or resident
description: A real-time motion alert can directly or indirectly identify a data subject by tying occupancy activity to a named account, address, device registration, or other backend-held profile data. Even if the alert itself contains little content, backend-side enrichment can identify the household or individuals associated with the home.
assumptions: The backend can associate the incoming alert with a customer account, home address, or user profile.
uncertainty_note: Node id is a best-fit estimate for identifiability via direct or indirect identifiers.

title: Real-time motion alerts disclose presence and behavioral patterns
description: The alert reveals that motion was detected at a specific time, which can expose sensitive information about presence at home, daily routines, occupancy schedules, sleeping patterns, or absence. If accessed beyond what is necessary, the backend processing of this flow can disclose private household behavior.
assumptions: The alert includes event timing and is retained, observable, or further shared within backend systems.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for disclosure of sensitive event content and inferred behavioral information.

title: Occupancy and lifestyle can be inferred from motion-alert streams
description: Even when a single alert seems innocuous, a stream of motion alerts enables inference of intimate facts such as work schedules, travel, religious observance, family composition, or health-related routines. The backend can derive more information than users may expect from the raw event feed.
assumptions: The backend stores or analyzes alert histories across time or combines them with other account/device data.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort mapping to an inference threat node; exact node id may differ across LINDDUN Pro versions.

title: Users may not expect backend processing of detailed motion events
description: Forwarding real-time motion alerts to the backend may exceed user expectations if the collection, retention, analytics, or onward use of occupancy events is not clearly communicated or consented to. This creates a risk that processing is not transparent or not aligned with the stated purpose.
assumptions: Not all users are fully informed about the backend's collection, retention, and use of motion-event telemetry.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for non-compliance/insufficient transparency or purpose limitation concerns; exact subtree may vary.

title: The hub or operator may be unable to prove what motion alert was sent and when
description: If the flow lacks reliable event integrity, timestamping, or audit evidence, the sender and receiver may later dispute whether a motion alert was generated, forwarded, modified, or delayed. This can undermine accountability for privacy-relevant event processing.
assumptions: Logging, secure timestamps, or integrity protections on event transmission are limited or incomplete.
uncertainty_note: Repudiation is less central than other privacy threats for this flow; node id is a best-effort estimate.

title: Notification content may disclose presence or occupancy information
description: A motion-detected push notification sent from the backend to the homeowner can reveal sensitive facts such as that someone is at home, away, or that movement occurred at a specific property. If the notification text is visible on the lock screen or to other people with access to the device, it can disclose personal information about household activity.
assumptions: Assumes the notification contains explicit motion-event details, device/location labels, or timing information and may be shown on the phone lock screen.
uncertainty_note: Tree node chosen as a generic information disclosure/content exposure node; exact LINDDUN Pro subnode may vary by catalog version.

title: Repeated motion alerts can enable linkage of homeowner behavior patterns
description: A series of motion-detected notifications delivered to the same homeowner device can be correlated over time to infer routines such as occupancy schedules, sleep patterns, travel, or periods of absence. Even if each alert seems innocuous, together they can be linked to build a detailed profile of the homeowner's behavior.
assumptions: Assumes notifications are retained in app history, notification center, backups, or accessible logs on the device.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit linkage node based on correlating multiple events to one data subject/device; exact subnode may differ in LINDDUN Pro.

title: Notification metadata can identify the homeowner or household
description: Push delivery metadata and notification content may identify the recipient as the resident of a specific monitored home or user of a home-security system. Device tokens, account identifiers, property labels, or personalized text can make the homeowner identifiable to service operators, push providers, or anyone viewing the notification.
assumptions: Assumes the push path involves provider-managed infrastructure and/or the notification includes user- or home-specific identifiers.
uncertainty_note: Node is selected as a generic identifiability threat; exact LINDDUN Pro node id may differ.

title: Homeowner may be unaware of notification recipients or visibility scope
description: The homeowner may not understand that motion notifications can appear on lock screens, wearables, shared devices, or be processed by third-party push services. This lack of awareness reduces the user's ability to make informed decisions about what event information is exposed and where.
assumptions: Assumes default notification settings or ecosystem integrations can surface alerts beyond the primary phone screen.
uncertainty_note: Mapped to a generic unawareness node because the main issue is insufficient user awareness of downstream disclosure/processing.

title: Motion-event notifications may be sent without sufficiently specific consent or preference control
description: If the backend sends detailed motion alerts by default, the processing and communication of occupancy-related data may exceed the homeowner's expectations or configured preferences. Users may want only generic alerts, quiet hours, or no lock-screen content, and absent such controls this flow can violate consent or choice requirements.
assumptions: Assumes consent/preferences for push notifications or detailed event content are not granularly managed.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit non-compliance/consent-related node; exact subnode may differ depending on the LINDDUN Pro tree version.

title: Notification previews on shared or compromised devices can expose household events to unauthorized viewers
description: When the homeowner's phone is shared with family members, visible to bystanders, connected to car displays, or compromised by malware, the motion-detected notification can disclose sensitive household events to parties other than the intended recipient.
assumptions: Assumes endpoint device access by others or preview mirroring to secondary surfaces.
uncertainty_note: Treated as disclosure at the recipient endpoint; exact node id may vary.

title: Shared analytics may remain linkable to individual devices or accounts
description: Although described as aggregated device-usage analytics, the dataset sent by the mobile app backend may still contain stable pseudonymous identifiers, small-cohort aggregates, timestamps, event combinations, or segmentation dimensions that allow the cloud analytics vendor to link records back to the same device, account, or household over time.
assumptions: The aggregation may preserve per-device, per-account, or fine-grained cohort dimensions, or the vendor may already hold related identifiers from other integrations.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id; exact LINDDUN Pro subnode for linkability of shared pseudonymous analytics may vary.

title: Aggregated usage data may enable inference about users or user segments
description: The cloud analytics vendor may infer behavioral patterns, interests, routines, app engagement levels, geographic habits, or sensitive traits from the shared analytics, especially when metrics are broken down by time, feature, region, device model, or other dimensions.
assumptions: The vendor can analyze the shared metrics in combination with its own models or other customer/platform data.
uncertainty_note: Node id is a best estimate for inference from observed/shared data.

title: Users may not be aware that backend analytics are disclosed to a third-party vendor
description: If the app's privacy notices or in-product disclosures do not clearly explain that aggregated device-usage analytics are sent from the backend to an external cloud analytics vendor, users may lack awareness of this disclosure and downstream processing.
assumptions: Notice is incomplete, hard to find, overly generic, or does not clearly identify third-party analytics sharing.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for lack of awareness/non-transparency regarding third-party disclosure.

title: Analytics data may be used for secondary purposes beyond the original app analytics purpose
description: Once received by the cloud analytics vendor, the shared analytics could be repurposed for service improvement, benchmarking, model training, product development, fraud detection, or other secondary purposes that exceed the users' original expectations or the controller's stated purpose.
assumptions: Contractual restrictions are weak, broad, or permit provider-side secondary use.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for purpose creep / use beyond user expectations.

title: Third-party analytics sharing may lack a valid legal basis or exceed declared purpose
description: Sending device-usage analytics to an external analytics vendor may be non-compliant if the controller lacks a valid legal basis, fails to honor consent/opt-out choices, transfers more detail than necessary, or does not align the disclosure with stated privacy terms and applicable jurisdictional requirements.
assumptions: Applicable law or policy requires consent, opt-out, minimization, transparency, contractual controls, or transfer safeguards for this type of analytics sharing.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for non-compliance in third-party analytics disclosure; exact subnode may differ by legal/control context.

title: Aggregated analytics may still permit identification in small groups or rare patterns
description: If aggregation is too granular, includes rare combinations, or covers small populations, the data sent to the vendor may still allow singling out or re-identification of an individual device, account, or small user group.
assumptions: The analytics include fine-grained dimensions, sparse cohorts, or high-cardinality attributes.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for identifiability/discoverability from insufficient aggregation.

title: Backend can infer viewing habits from video retrieval requests
description: When the mobile app backend retrieves specific stored video clips for playback, the backend can observe which cameras, timestamps, and events the homeowner chooses to view. This reveals behavioral patterns, occupancy routines, and interests beyond what is strictly necessary to transport the clip.
assumptions: P2 has access to identifiers for the user, camera, clip, and request timing, and these accesses may be logged or analyzed.
uncertainty_note: Tree node id is my best fit for inference from access/request metadata; exact LINDDUN Pro sub-node may differ.

title: Video retrieval requests are linkable to the same homeowner across sessions
description: Repeated retrieval of stored clips through the backend can be linked to the same account, device, household, or camera set. This enables construction of a long-term profile of the homeowner's surveillance usage and activity patterns.
assumptions: Stable account IDs, device IDs, session tokens, or camera identifiers are available to P2 or in associated logs.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for linkability via persistent identifiers/session metadata; exact sub-node may vary.

title: Backend learns that a specific homeowner requested playback of a specific clip
description: The act of retrieving a clip from cloud storage to the backend may disclose the homeowner's identity or account in connection with a particular video, camera location, or event time. This can expose sensitive household activities and security-related events to backend operators or internal systems.
assumptions: The retrieval is associated with an authenticated account or household identifier and clip metadata is accessible at P2.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for identity disclosure through authenticated retrieval context; exact sub-node may differ.

title: Stored clip content discloses personal information when accessed for playback
description: The video clip itself can contain identifiable individuals, visitors, household members, routines, possessions, or location cues. When DS2 serves the clip to P2, this sensitive content is exposed to any component or operator with access along that path.
assumptions: DS2 stores raw or only lightly transformed video and P2 can access the content or derived metadata.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for disclosure of sensitive data content; exact LINDDUN Pro node id is uncertain.

title: Homeowner may be unaware of backend-side access and secondary processing during playback retrieval
description: A homeowner may believe playback is a direct fetch of their clip, while the backend may log, inspect, cache, transcode, or analyze the video retrieval. If this processing is not transparent, the user may be insufficiently informed about how their data is handled.
assumptions: The service performs server-side processing or logging not fully explained in the user-facing notice.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for lack of awareness/transparency; exact sub-node may differ.

title: Playback retrieval may exceed the purpose or legal basis communicated to the homeowner
description: If clip retrieval through the backend is also used for analytics, service improvement, employee review, or law-enforcement preparation beyond delivering playback, the processing may be non-compliant with stated purposes, data minimization, or applicable legal obligations.
assumptions: Backend retrievals or associated logs are reused for secondary purposes not strictly necessary for playback.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for non-compliance with purpose limitation or transparency obligations; exact node id may differ.

title: Insufficient evidence about who accessed which stored clip
description: If retrieval events are not reliably logged with actor, time, clip ID, and purpose, the service may be unable to prove whether a homeowner, support staff, or another internal actor accessed a specific video. This undermines accountability for privacy-sensitive playback access.
assumptions: Audit logging or integrity protection of access records is incomplete or absent.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for repudiation due to insufficient auditability; exact sub-node may vary.
